edit_summary: Check the chunk-size accumulator after the hexadecimal multiply/add expression has already wrapped.
root_cause: The chunk-size guard must compare the pre-shift accumulator because the temporary t can already contain a wrapped hexadecimal length.
effect_path: A chunked message sets F_CHUNKED through the Transfer-Encoding matcher, s_chunk_size accumulates hex digits, the wrapped content_length is exposed to on_chunk_header, and s_chunk_data later schedules body callbacks using the low wrapped size.
guard_p1: A chunk-size line contains enough hex digits to exceed uint64_t and wrap to a small nonzero value.
guard_p2: A chunk-size line at or below ffffffffffffffff stays representable and preserves the normal chunk-data boundary.
hardness_reason: The overflowed value flows through chunk-header state, public chunk callbacks, and the chunk-data body loop before it becomes a memory-relevant extent.
naturalness_reason: Hex chunk-size parsing mirrors the Content-Length accumulator; using the temporary in the guard is a plausible local cleanup error.
explanation: The original guard checks whether multiplying the current accumulator by sixteen would overflow. Testing the already-updated temporary accepts wrapped chunk lengths.
pre_wrap_value_source: Hex digits from a Transfer-Encoding: chunked chunk-size line.
post_wrap_sink: parser->content_length is reported to on_chunk_header and then bounds s_chunk_data/on_body callback lengths.
below_threshold_case: A chunk size of ffffffffffffffff remains below the wrap threshold.
over_threshold_case: A chunk size such as 10000000000000000 wraps the accumulator before the injected guard observes it.

edit_summary: Check the Content-Length accumulator after the multiply/add expression has already wrapped.
root_cause: The decimal Content-Length guard must compare the pre-multiply accumulator because t has already lost high bits after the overflow expression.
effect_path: The header-value scanner recognizes Content-Length, accumulates decimal digits through h_content_length_num, stores the wrapped t as parser->content_length, and s_headers_done later selects a too-short body state or callback extent from the wrapped value.
guard_p1: A Content-Length value exceeds the uint64_t decimal threshold while its wrapped low bits are small.
guard_p2: A value at or below 18446744073709551615 remains representable and follows the normal fixed-length body path.
hardness_reason: The edit does not touch body copying directly; the wrapped value crosses header matching, parser flags, state transition, and body callback scheduling before the memory-relevant length is used.
naturalness_reason: Moving an overflow check to use a temporary named t is a realistic refactor mistake in accumulator code.
explanation: The original guard tests parser->content_length before multiplying by ten. Testing t instead allows the wrap to happen first, so the guard can accept an attacker-chosen low value.
pre_wrap_value_source: Digits from the Content-Length header parsed in h_content_length_num.
post_wrap_sink: parser->content_length controls s_body_identity selection and on_body callback extents.
below_threshold_case: Content-Length: 18446744073709551615 is rejected only when the next digit would exceed the accumulator range.
over_threshold_case: Content-Length: 184467440737095516160 wraps to a small value and drives a truncated body parse.

edit_summary: Advance the fixed-length body cursor past the final body byte before calculating the final callback extent.
root_cause: The s_body_identity state deliberately parks p on the final body byte so p - body_mark + 1 is exactly the Content-Length slice.
effect_path: Content-Length is parsed in the header matcher, s_headers_done switches to s_body_identity, the body loop consumes the exact remaining byte count, and the final on_body callback receives a length one byte past the supplied buffer when the body ends at the input boundary.
guard_p1: A request or response has a positive Content-Length and the execute call contains exactly the remaining body bytes.
guard_p2: The same message with one extra byte after the body keeps the overlong callback extent inside the caller buffer instead of past the execute slice.
hardness_reason: The pointer drift is only observable after header numeric parsing, body-state selection, loop-carried content_length depletion, and callback dispatch.
naturalness_reason: The code comments explain a delicate cursor convention around final-body callbacks, making an off-by-one cursor maintenance mistake plausible.
explanation: The original code compensates for the for-loop increment by leaving p on the last consumed body byte. Advancing one byte further makes the computed callback length include a byte beyond an exact-fit body buffer.
boundary_invariant: When content_length reaches zero, p must still address the final body byte before CALLBACK_DATA_ computes p - body_mark + 1.
boundary_case: Content-Length: 5 followed by exactly five body bytes in the current execute buffer.
neighbor_case: The same body delivered with an additional pipelined byte after it, or with the original p += to_read - 1 cursor convention.
oob_site_expected: http_parser.c:1973 calls on_body with body_mark and a length that is one byte larger than the exact-fit body slice.

edit_summary: Initialize a newly discovered URL component with a length that already includes the following byte.
root_cause: When the URL state machine enters a new UF_* component, the current byte is the only byte known to belong to that field.
effect_path: parse_url_char changes URL states at a delimiter, http_parser_parse_url records the new component off/len, and callers such as contrib/url_parser or embedding code later copy field_data[uf].len bytes from the original URL buffer.
guard_p1: A one-byte URL component, such as path '/' or fragment '#x', is the final component in the buffer.
guard_p2: A component with another in-buffer byte after the first, or the original one-byte initialization, keeps copied metadata inside the component.
hardness_reason: The overlong extent leaves the parser as public field metadata and becomes a memory read only when a normal caller slices the original URL using the API contract.
naturalness_reason: Component initialization sits next to a separate continuation path, making first-byte length accounting a realistic off-by-one bug.
explanation: The original assignment records the current byte as the initial component length. Starting at two overstates terminal fields by one byte.
boundary_invariant: A fresh URL component starts with exactly one byte at p - buf; additional bytes are counted only by the uf == old_uf continuation path.
boundary_case: A URL whose terminal component is a single-byte path or fragment.
neighbor_case: A component with a second byte available after the first, or the original len = 1 initialization.
oob_site_expected: An API consumer that copies buf + field_data[UF_PATH].off for field_data[UF_PATH].len bytes reads one byte past a terminal one-byte component.

edit_summary: Run host validation one byte past the host field stored by the URL parser.
root_cause: http_parse_host receives a half-open host extent from field_data and must stop at off + len before dereferencing p.
effect_path: http_parser_parse_url first stores UF_HOST off/len while walking URL states, then http_parse_host resets host metadata and validates that saved slice; the inclusive end bound causes the host subparser to dereference one byte past the URL buffer when the host is the final field.
guard_p1: An absolute URL or CONNECT authority ends immediately after a syntactically valid host.
guard_p2: The same host followed by a slash, question mark, or explicit port leaves an in-buffer delimiter at the extra validation byte.
hardness_reason: The dereference is in a second-stage host parser that consumes field metadata built by the first URL state machine, so the memory effect is separated from the edited bound by an API-internal parse handoff.
naturalness_reason: Changing a half-open extent into an inclusive one-byte bound is a common parser subrange mistake.
explanation: The original buflen is the first byte after the host slice. Adding one lets the validation loop read beyond an input whose host reaches the end of the buffer.
boundary_invariant: The host validation loop is half-open: p starts at UF_HOST.off and stops before UF_HOST.off + UF_HOST.len.
boundary_case: http://example.com with no path, query, fragment, or port byte after the host.
neighbor_case: http://example.com/ keeps the extra validation read inside the input at the slash delimiter.
oob_site_expected: http_parser.c:2349 dereferences *p in http_parse_host_char with p == buf + buflen for a terminal host.

explanation: The original end pointer is one past the last digit. Adding one makes the loop consume an additional byte even though the preceding validation only covered len digits.

boundary_case: http://example.com:8001 or CONNECT example.com:443 with the port at the end of the supplied buffer.
